key_insight: Cap-and-Track adapts LLM inference dispatch to shifting capacity using admission refusals, without predicting output length or retuning a fleet-wide rate.
engineering_relevance: Separating durable waiting queues from inference execution can reduce GPU requirements while adapting to changing workloads and backend capacity.
method: Cap refuses requests at the saturated resource before long execution-side waits form.
Track probes upward and backs off using capacity refusals alone.
Durable priority queues hold excess and refused requests for later dispatch.
evidence_signal: A concurrent production A/B served a classifier on 43% fewer H100s than the queued, fixed-rate precursor; steady-capacity real-engine replay achieved goodput within 1% of an above-capacity fixed rate with about one-quarter of its refusal share.
watch_item: Lower-priority work waited longer during backfill peaks, so fleet sizing must account for acceptable queueing delays.
paper_title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
